# Pool 0.11.0
- Adds CURRENT, a shared ledger for open-ended projects, weekly attention, bounded work, and immutable receipts. - Gives each member 100 fresh, non-transferable attention points per week while preserving individual allocations and disagreement. - Keeps project purpose, desired outcome, privacy, lane, resource envelope, and every revision together. - Lets stewards propose and approve allowlisted work orders with explicit caps for agent tokens, GPU minutes, retained storage, and cloud spend. - Matches queued work to opt-in providers by recipe and administrator-set privacy trust, with renewable leases and safe crash recovery. - Runs provider-local recipes without exposing Pool member or worker tokens to child processes, stops full process groups at timeout, and retains capped artifacts with hashes. - Keeps CURRENT independent from Images, Press, and Links permissions, so the institution can be shared without exposing the studio archive.

p∞l 0.8.0 makes KILN a true in-app instrument. Members granted KILN access can open and use it directly from Pool's top navigation without installing or launching a second application. KILN inherits the member's existing Pool token, renders locally, retains the established local firing archive, and downloads only selected team source originals. Starred firings continue to preserve their recipes, inputs, recovery bundles, and Pool project records.
This release removes the former KILN installer and launcher path. Per-person visibility remains controlled by the team server, so members without a KILN grant neither see the tab nor reach its local APIs.

p∞l 0.7.4 can carry KILN as an optional, verified companion application. Members with KILN access can install and open it directly from the KILN tab; Pool copies only the application into that member's own Applications folder and does not bundle or download the KILN firing archive.
